about-hero-subtitle: Trusted global leader in power system design, protection, and control
about-content: At PSAI POWER, we are a trusted global leader in power system design, protection, and control. With extensive experience across diverse regions, including North America, Latin America, the Caribbean, and Asia, we have successfully delivered innovative, reliable, and cost-effective power solutions for utilities, mines, and industrial clients.
about-mission-body: We pride ourselves on our customer-centric approach, working closely with clients to develop tailored solutions that meet their specific needs. Our team is dedicated to delivering innovative power measurement and protection instruments that are easy to install and ensure minimal outage durations.
about-vision-body: We go beyond traditional approaches to bring forward-thinking technologies that improve both the performance and reliability of power systems while minimizing disruptions. Our goal is to lead the industry in advanced grid optimization, renewable energy integration, and cutting-edge protection schemes.
about-expertise-body: Our expertise spans a wide range of power system applications, including Distributed Energy Resource (DER) interconnections to the distribution grid with successful integrations up to 150MW. We understand the unique challenges each project presents and approach each one with a deep understanding of the technical and regulatory environments.
contact-hero-subtitle: We're here to help. Reach out to us for any inquiries or to discuss your next project.
contact-status-success: Thank you for your message! We will get back to you soon.
resource-technical-whitepapers-content: Access our library of technical whitepapers covering advanced power system design, protection schemes, grid modernization strategies, and renewable energy integration methodologies. These documents represent our cutting-edge research and practical implementations across North America.
resource-case-studies-content: Explore real-world case studies showcasing our successful power system projects. Learn about our work with utilities, industrial clients, and renewable energy providers. Each case study details the challenges faced, solutions implemented, and results achieved.
resource-integration-guides-content: Comprehensive guides for Distributed Energy Resource (DER) interconnections, renewable energy integration, and grid modernization. These technical documents provide step-by-step instructions, best practices, and regulatory compliance information.
resource-compliance-documents-content: Access regulatory compliance documentation, standards adherence guidelines, and certification materials. Ensure your power systems meet all necessary industry standards and governmental regulations.
resource-technical-briefs-content: Concise technical briefs covering specific power system topics, innovative solutions, and emerging technologies. Perfect for quick reference and staying updated with industry advancements.
resource-best-practices-content: Industry best practices for power system maintenance, optimization, and reliability. These documents compile decades of experience into actionable guidelines for optimal system performance.
resource-access-content: Contact us to request access to our full resource library or schedule a technical consultation.

careers-hero-subtitle: Help build reliable, modern power systems for utilities, industry, and mines across Canada.
careers-intro: PSAI POWER is a growing power engineering consultancy. You'll work directly on real substations, industrial plants, and renewable projects — with senior engineers who mentor, a safety-first culture, and room to grow with the practice.
careers-eligibility: Applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada (Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or valid work permit holder). We are unable to sponsor work visas at this time.
careers-apply-note: Send your resume and a short introduction to
careers-eng-summary: We're looking for an intermediate electrical engineer to grow with our power systems consulting practice. You'll work across power systems studies, protection and control, substation design, and commissioning and testing, as well as industrial medium- and low-voltage electrical design, control, and automation — supporting projects from concept through detailed design to site energization for utility, renewable, and mining clients.
careers-eng-r1: Perform power system studies — load flow, short circuit, protection coordination, arc flash, and grounding — using ETAP or similar tools
careers-eng-r2: Develop protection and control designs for MV/HV substations, including relay selection and settings
careers-eng-r3: Prepare design deliverables: single-line diagrams, layouts, schematics, equipment specifications, and cable schedules
careers-eng-r4: Design industrial MV/LV power distribution, motor control, and automation systems (MCCs, VFDs, PLC/SCADA interfaces)
careers-eng-r5: Support factory and site acceptance testing, commissioning, and energization
careers-eng-r6: Coordinate with other disciplines, vendors, contractors, and clients from concept to close-out
careers-eng-q1: Bachelor's degree (4-year) in Electrical Engineering, or CET diploma with equivalent experience
careers-eng-q2: 3–5 years of relevant experience in power systems, substation, or industrial electrical design
careers-eng-q3: Registered EIT with a Canadian engineering association preferred; P.Eng designation is an asset, not required
careers-eng-q4: Working knowledge of applicable codes and standards (CEC, CSA, IEEE)
careers-eng-q5: Clear communication in reports, drawings, and client-facing discussions
careers-eng-a1: Hands-on experience with ETAP, AutoCAD, and relay programming tools
careers-eng-a2: Field exposure to commissioning or testing of MV/HV equipment
careers-tech-title: Electrical Field Technician — Substations, MV/LV Equipment, Pumps & Motors
careers-tech-summary: We're seeking an electrical field technician to support field installation, inspection, testing, commissioning, troubleshooting, and maintenance of electrical equipment in power substations and industrial facilities — working on medium- and low-voltage systems including transformers, switchgear, breakers, protection relays, MCCs, VFDs, motors, and pumps.
careers-tech-r1: Inspect, test, commission, and maintain substations, MV/LV switchgear, transformers, breakers, CTs/PTs, and control panels
careers-tech-r2: Perform point-to-point wiring checks, breaker timing, insulation and contact resistance, ratio and polarity tests, and energization checks
careers-tech-r3: Troubleshoot and maintain motors, pumps, MCCs, VFDs, soft starters, and motor control circuits
careers-tech-r4: Work with multimeters, insulation testers, low-resistance ohmmeters, relay test sets, phase rotation and power quality meters
careers-tech-r5: Read single-lines, schematics, and wiring diagrams; prepare field reports, deficiency lists, and as-built markups
careers-tech-r6: Follow lockout/tagout, arc-flash boundaries, permit-to-work processes, and site electrical safety rules
careers-tech-q1: Electrical Technician or Technologist diploma, or equivalent electrical trade and field experience
careers-tech-q2: 3–7 years of hands-on field experience with industrial electrical systems, substations, motors, or commissioning
careers-tech-q3: Ability to read and interpret electrical drawings and equipment manuals
careers-tech-q4: Strong understanding of lockout/tagout and electrical safety procedures
careers-tech-q5: Valid driver's licence and willingness to travel to field sites
careers-tech-a1: Substation experience from 4.16 kV to 44 kV, 69 kV or higher
careers-tech-a2: Experience with SEL, GE Multilin, Siemens, Schneider Electric, Eaton, or ABB relays and equipment
careers-tech-a3: Omicron, Doble, Megger, or Vanguard test sets; protection scheme testing
careers-tech-a4: Red Seal licence or CET designation; WHMIS, First Aid, Confined Space, or mine-site safety training
pp-intro: {legalName} ("{shortName}", "we", "us") is a power system engineering firm in Sudbury, Ontario. This policy explains what personal information we collect through this website and by email, why we collect it, who else handles it, and what you can ask of us. We handle personal information in accordance with the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA).
pp-collect-form-body: Your name, email address, a subject, your message, and — only if you choose to tell us — how you heard about us. Nothing else is required, and nothing is collected from the form until you press send.
pp-collect-email-body: If you write to {email} or call us, we receive whatever you choose to include, along with your email address or phone number.
pp-collect-careers-body: Applications are sent by email. We receive your résumé, cover letter, contact details, and anything you tell us about your eligibility to work in Canada.
pp-collect-analytics-body: We use Vercel Web Analytics to count visits in aggregate: which pages are viewed, the referring site, and the country, device type and browser of each visit. It does not use cookies, and it is not used to identify you or to advertise to you.
pp-use-body: To answer your enquiry, to discuss and scope a possible engagement, to assess a job application, and to understand which pages are useful so we can improve the site. We use your information only for the purpose you gave it to us for. We do not sell, rent or trade personal information, and we do not send marketing email.
pp-confidential-body: The contact form is meant for a first enquiry. It is not a secure channel for drawings, relay settings, study reports or anything else that is confidential to you or your client. Tell us what you have, and we will agree with you how to receive it. Once an engagement begins, confidential material is governed by the confidentiality terms of that agreement.
pp-providers-body: Two service providers process information on our behalf, only to provide their service to us: Vercel Inc. hosts this website and provides the analytics described above, and Formspree Inc. receives contact form submissions and forwards them to us by email. Both are based in the United States and may store information there, where it can be subject to United States law, including lawful access by courts and authorities. Job applications and direct email are handled through our own email service. Links to Google Maps and LinkedIn take you to those sites, which have their own privacy policies.
pp-cookies-body: This website sets no cookies and stores nothing in your browser. There is no cookie banner because there is nothing to consent to.
pp-retention-body: We keep enquiries for as long as we need them to respond and, if we work together, for the life of the business relationship and the records we are required to keep as a professional engineering firm. We keep job applications while the role is open and, only if you agree, to consider you for a later opening. When information is no longer needed, we delete it.
pp-safeguards-body: Access to personal information is limited to the people at the firm who need it to do their work. The site is served only over an encrypted connection. If a breach of our safeguards creates a real risk of significant harm to you, we will notify you and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, as the law requires.
pp-rights-body1: You can ask to see the personal information we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or withdraw your consent to our using it. Write to our privacy officer at
pp-rights-body2: We will respond within 30 days. If you are not satisfied with our answer, you can complain to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada at priv.gc.ca.
pp-changes-body: If we change how we handle personal information, we will update this page and the date at the top of it.
tos-intro: These terms govern your use of the website of {legalName} ("{shortName}", "we", "us"). By using this website you agree to them. If you do not agree, please do not use the site.
tos-info-body: The content on this website describes our services and our general approach to engineering problems. It is not engineering advice, a professional opinion, or a deliverable for any project, and it must not be relied on as one. Every power system is different, and engineering judgement depends on the specific system, its data, and the applicable codes. Do not make design, protection, safety or operating decisions based on this website.
tos-relationship-body: Contacting us through this website, by email or by phone does not create an engineer–client relationship, and does not oblige us to take on any work. That relationship begins only when both parties sign a written agreement, and our services are then governed by that agreement rather than by these terms.
tos-licensure-body: In Canada, engineering services are provided by, or under the direct supervision of, professional engineers licensed in the province where the work is carried out. Only work that bears the seal of a licensed professional engineer should be treated as an engineering document.
tos-ip-body: Unless otherwise noted, the text, diagrams, figures, logos and other content on this site belong to {legalName} or its licensors and are protected by Canadian and international copyright law. You may view and print pages for your own reference. You may not reproduce, republish or redistribute them without our written permission.
tos-submissions-body: Please do not send us confidential or proprietary material before we have agreed how to receive it. We cannot treat unsolicited material as confidential until an agreement is in place.
tos-warranty-body: This website is provided "as is". We work to keep it accurate, but we do not warrant that its content is complete, current or free of errors, or that the site will always be available.
tos-liability-body: To the fullest extent permitted by law, {legalName} is not liable for any loss or damage arising from your use of, or inability to use, this website or its content. Nothing in these terms limits any liability that cannot be limited under applicable law.
tos-links-body: This site links to other websites, such as Google Maps and LinkedIn. We are not responsible for their content or their privacy practices.
tos-changes-body: We may update these terms. The date at the top of this page shows when they last changed, and the version published here is the one that applies.
tos-law-body: These terms are governed by the laws of the Province of Ontario and the federal laws of Canada that apply there. Any dispute will be heard in the courts of Ontario.
a11y-intro: {legalName} is committed to making this website usable by everyone, including people who use a screen reader, a keyboard instead of a mouse, magnification, or reduced-motion settings. We follow the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) and design to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, level AA.
a11y-done-1: You can move through the site with a keyboard alone. The first stop on every page is a "Skip to content" link, and whatever has focus is always outlined.
a11y-done-2: Text and interface colours meet WCAG AA contrast ratios against their backgrounds.
a11y-done-3: Each page has one main heading and a logical heading order, so screen readers can navigate by section.
a11y-done-4: The fault diagram on the home page describes its current state in text, and the toggle announces which scenario is shown.
a11y-done-5: If your system asks for reduced motion, the diagram appears fully drawn, without animation.
a11y-done-6: Pages reflow to a single column on screens as narrow as 360 pixels, without sideways scrolling.
a11y-done-7: Automated tests check these properties whenever the site’s code changes.
a11y-limits-body: Some technical figures, such as time-current coordination curves, carry information that is hard to express fully in text. Each has a written caption that states its main point. If you need the detail behind a figure, ask us and we will explain it or provide it another way.
a11y-formats-body: Any information on this website is available on request in an accessible format or with communication support, at no cost to you. Tell us what works for you and we will arrange it with you.
a11y-feedback-body: If something on this site does not work for you, we want to know. Tell us which page, what you were trying to do, and what happened, by email at {email} or by phone. We will reply, fix what we can, and give you the information you were looking for in another way in the meantime.
